Nina — thanks for the topology and traffic sample. Quick responses and proposed baseline below. Happy to take the sync — Tue 2027-04-27 09:30 PT works for me.

Sustained baseline recommendation (first-phase):
- Target sustained throughput: ~45k tokens/sec aggregate across the pool (~5k tokens/sec per GPU node if using p4d-equivalent instances).
- Latency SLO to design for: 95th <= 120ms for typical 32-token generations (this drives batching and instance sizing).
- Burst headroom: reserve 1.6x capacity for predictable surges; auto-burst to 2.2x for short windows (30s–2m) with admission control.

Network / egress guidance:
- Plan for 10–12 Gbps egress per GPU node for mixed request shapes; 40 Gbps per rack should be fine but verify cross-rack aggregation and any per-AZ peering caps.
- If you expect long-form generation (avg 200 tokens), multiply node network needs by ~4–5x.

Validation checklist (minimum):
1) KV cache warmup script and cache-hit benchmark (attach warmup CSV).
2) Synthetic traffic run at 1.2x baseline sustained for 30m to validate autoscale and throttles.
3) End-to-end latency trace sampling under representative sequences.

I've attached a short capacity estimate workbook (redwood-capacity-estimates-20270422.xlsx) with sample math and node-count projections. Come prepared with expected avg seq length per endpoint and p95 request concurrency.

See you Tue 04/27 09:30 PT — invite to follow.

—Dylan

Nina / Dylan — adding network-level specifics and a compact sizing heuristic so your ops team can run quick checks before the sync.

Network constraints and practical sizing notes:
- Per-GPU egress: assume 8–14 Gbps under typical generation workloads (short form 16–32 tokens). If you have transformers with long context windows or batching that favors bigger sequences, budget toward the upper bound.
- Cross-AZ latency: keep inter-AZ RTT <3ms for node-to-cache synchronization; anything above adds jitter that amplifies p95 latency.

Quick sizing heuristic (rule-of-thumb you can run locally):
- node_throughput_tps (tokens/sec) = measured_single_node_token_rate (run our microbench) * cache_hit_factor
- estimated_nodes = ceil((expected_peak_RPS * avg_seq_len) / node_throughput_tps) * (safety_factor)

Example (from our workbook):
- expected_peak_RPS = 220 requests/sec (mixed endpoints)
- avg_seq_len = 48 tokens
- measured_single_node_token_rate = 5,000 tokens/sec (perf run with 32-token median)
- cache_hit_factor = 1.12 (12% gain with KV cache warm hits)
- safety_factor = 1.6 (headroom)

calculation: nodes = ceil((220 * 48) / (5000 * 1.12)) * 1.6 ≈ ceil(9.43) * 1.6 ≈ 10 * 1.6 => 16 nodes

Operational notes:
- Warmup: assume 6–12 minutes to reach stable KV-cache hit rates after cold start for common prefixes (plan warmup sequences at deployment cutover).
- Admission control: prefer graceful shedding at the edge with 429s on excess non-critical endpoints vs queue growth inside GPU worker processes.

Vivek — can your team confirm typical single-node network egress observed for our p4-equivalent footprints (we should put measured numbers in the workbook before Tue)?

Irene

Quick add from infra: measured egress and autoscale behavior notes.

Measured numbers (p4-like instance) from recent internal runs:
- sustained token rate (median): 4,900–5,300 tokens/sec depending on model quantization and batch window.
- network egress observed: 9–11 Gbps under small-to-medium sequences (<=64 tokens); peaks up to 18 Gbps when encoding long sessions and heavy streaming.

Autoscale guidance:
- Use reactive autoscaler keyed on pooled token throughput + per-node GPU occupancy (not just CPU or network).
- Warm pool: maintain 10% of baseline node count as warm idle nodes to bring down cold-start tail latencies.

I'll attach a short CSV of measured runs to the drive link (internal reference). We'll dump the p50/p95 token throughput numbers into your workbook by EOD Monday so you have measured inputs for the heuristic Irene outlined.
